units: Report task counts and source-group counts separately; related queries are not independent sources.
splitRule: All related sources, derivatives and paraphrases belong to one group and split. Development and holdout groups cannot overlap.
labels: File and locator labels are authored from source contents before inference. Filenames are opaque. Do not generate labels from retrieved predictions.
negativeRule: A negative task has no supported source in the searched corpus. Any admitted file is a false admission.
ambiguousRule: Report acceptable-file recall and advertised certainty separately; do not count ambiguous tasks in unambiguous first-file accuracy.
freezeRule: Hash the dataset and every source, record this protocol hash, and refuse changes after freezing. Preserve the exact source bytes, including synthetic speech.
baselineRule: Run current keyword content search, semantic-only and production fusion separately. Laya receives only the production metadata shortlist.
holdoutRule: Do not tune against opened holdout results. A failed opened holdout becomes regression evidence; a fresh independent holdout is required for a subsequent release claim.
limits: A small development pilot, toy visuals, synthetic speech or filename-only benchmarks cannot establish general content quality. Record corpus coverage and missing real-media slices.
releaseRule: Quality evaluation does not prove release readiness: physical 16 GB CPU, resource, packaged lifecycle, distribution and clean-account gates remain separate.
